title: Z-Wave Everspring ST814 no longer updates temperature or humidity
body:
### The problem

Using Z-Wave JS 0.1.34

The ST814 no longer reports temperature or humidity settings although it is reporting a wakeup every hour in the logs.

The ST814 never used to work then a fix was put in place in HA and in the logs I used to see this reported:
```
2021-04-14T13:15:41.023Z CNTRLR [Node 028] Mapping unsolicited report from root device to first supporting end
point #1
```

I no longer see these messages and suspect that may help to determine what has happened.

A link to another person with the same issue and additional debug information is available [here](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/everspring-st814-temp-humidity-stop-to-update/326920/1)


### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.8.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Z-Wave JS

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/zwave_js/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Thanks for the logs.

There's a mismatch between the endpoint that the values are sent from, and endpoint of the value that the driver tells HA about. This results in the corresponding HA entities not being updated.

This is what HA knows about for Air temperature. It uses this value to create the sensor entity. Notice it's endpoint 1.

```json
    {
      "endpoint": 1,
      "commandClass": 49,
      "commandClassName": "Multilevel Sensor",
      "property": "Air temperature",
      "propertyName": "Air temperature",
      "ccVersion": 2,
      "metadata": {
        "type": "number",
        "readable": true,
        "writeable": false,
        "label": "Air temperature",
        "ccSpecific": {
          "sensorType": 1,
          "scale": 1
        },
        "unit": "°F"
      },
      "value": 73.4
    }
```

And here is the unsolicited Air temperature report from the last log. In this instance, the report comes from endpoint 0.

```text
2021-09-12T08:35:09.250Z SERIAL « 0x010c00040018063105012200ed13                                      (14 bytes)
2021-09-12T08:35:09.253Z CNTRLR   [Node 024] [Multilevel Sensor] Air temperature: metadata updated  [Endpoint 0]
2021-09-12T08:35:09.254Z CNTRLR   [Node 024] [~] [Multilevel Sensor] Air temperature: 24.7 => 23.7  [Endpoint 0]
2021-09-12T08:35:09.255Z SERIAL » [ACK]                                                                   (0x06)
2021-09-12T08:35:09.256Z DRIVER « [Node 024] [REQ] [ApplicationCommand]
                                  └─[MultilevelSensorCCReport]
                                      type:  Air temperature
                                      scale: Celsius
                                      value: 23.7
```

Because of this endpoint mismatch, that value that HA uses for the entity is not updated. The driver needs to address this, either by mapping endpoint 0 reports to endpoint 1, or some other means.

I believe the manual refresh is issuing a Get with endpoint 1/2 as the target, so the node probably responds properly in that case, but for it looks like unsolicited reports (usually?) come from endpoint 0.

@participant5 I think this issue is in your domain now, should a new one be created at node-zwave-js?

You would have to use standalone zwavejs2mqtt to test an updated config file, unless you know how to access the docker internals of the addons. zwavejs2mqtt has a `store/config` directory where you can add config files that override the embedded ones.

All config files are easily accessible via their DB entries. Click on the "View on Github" link. https://devices.zwave-js.io/?jumpTo=0x0060:0x0006:0x0001:0.0

Node 47

Looks like it. I have recently fixed something in that regard, but obviously you don't have access to the change yet.
If you have access to zwavejs2mqtt, you can add node 1 to association group 1 of the device.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body: I have been monitoring this issue, as I have these devices which were not updating as stated.  After the Zwave JS add-on in Home Assistant  is updated to 0.1.46 ("bump Zwave JS to 8.7.5", and "bump Zwave JS server to 1.10.8") I re-interviewed two devices and both are now updating as expected.
